decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: **Compile-time substitution:** define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`. ... **Runtime substitution:** define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` without the two macros. | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair. Defining the runtime option "without the two macros", and the macros omitting the runtime code in `platform.c`, shows they are mutually exclusive. || QUOTE: **Compile-time substitution:** define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`. `platform.h:139-144` then maps `mbedtls_calloc`/`mbedtls_free` to your macros, and `platform.c:20-22` omits its runtime code. ... **Runtime substitution:** define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` without the two macros. | WHY: The answer separates compile-time macro pair from runtime function-pointer pair, and says the runtime code is omitted when the macros are defined, plus "without the two macros" for runtime, which conveys that the two are mutually exclusive. || QUOTE: **Compile-time substitution:** define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`. ... **Runtime substitution:** define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` without the two macros. | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair. It says runtime substitution applies "without the two macros", and that `platform.c` omits its runtime code when the macros are defined. Together these state that the two are mutually exclusive.

decisions.mark: states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `platform.h:139-144` then maps `mbedtls_calloc`/`mbedtls_free` to your macros, and `platform.c:20-22` omits its runtime code. | WHY: The answer says the platform.c runtime code is omitted on the macro path. decisions.mark: identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
decisions.detail: QUOTE: If `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_STD_CALLOC` is undefined, the default is a stub that returns NULL, so allocation fails until you set a function (`mbedtls_config.h:4113-4134`). | WHY: The answer says the calloc default is a stub that returns NULL, but it never says the uninitialised free does nothing. The item needs both halves: calloc returns NULL and free is a no-op. || QUOTE: If `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_STD_CALLOC` is undefined, the default is a stub that returns NULL, so allocation fails until you set a function | WHY: The answer says the calloc stub returns NULL, but it never says the uninitialised free does nothing. The item needs both halves. || QUOTE: If `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_STD_CALLOC` is undefined, the default is a stub that returns NULL, so allocation fails until you set a function | WHY: The answer says the calloc default is a NULL-returning stub, but it never says the free default does nothing. The item needs both halves of the failure-not-fallback mechanism.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`library/memory_buffer_alloc.c:566-600`) manages a caller-supplied static buffer and installs its own `calloc`/`free` through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free`. | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator installs itself via the setter from its init function, but it never says it is the only in-tree user. It also lists the example programs (ssl_server2, benchmark and others) as using the allocator, and that doesn't establish exclusivity. || QUOTE: Ships its own allocator on top of the hook. `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`library/memory_buffer_alloc.c:566-600`) manages a caller-supplied static buffer and installs its own `calloc`/`free` through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free`. | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator installs itself via the setter from its init function, but it never says it is the only in-tree user, and it lists programs that use the allocator.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "installs its own `calloc`/`free` through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free`. It also says the function installs its own plain calloc/free pair, which covers the otherwise-plain case. It doesn't spell out "chosen at compile time", but the macro condition implies that. || QUOTE: "installs its own `calloc`/`free` through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free`.
